results.name: Async readback submits two passes synchronously and restores every caller state before its promise settles
Delayed result returns the supplied RGBA8 buffer and uses submission-time ACES exposure without changing later main-view state
One in-flight frame rejects sync/async reentry and disposal until completion without another draw or release
Deferred readback rejection restores pending lifetime and allows a subsequent successful frame
Source draw, display draw and asynchronous readback submission failures restore state immediately and do not poison reuse
A synchronous legacy renderer has an explicit compatible Promise fallback with unchanged color and restoration contracts
Fallback readback errors restore all state and preserve later synchronous and asynchronous fallback use
Async buffer/exposure/mapping validation rejects before any renderer mutation or read submission
Nested entry from either source/display draw cannot corrupt the enclosing asynchronous submission
Sync and async paths reuse identical HDR/display targets, bundled shader, geometry and material across exposure changes
Successful async disposal is idempotent, owns exactly four resources, and rejects all subsequent entry
Pass remains confined to existing renderer/targets with no context, canvas, robot or physical-world ownership

scope: Actual production camera-feed module with controlled asynchronous renderer-contract fixtures. Immediate restoration, deferred buffer/Promise lifetime, errors, reentry, disposal, fallback, original shader/color pipeline, resource reuse and ownership are tested. CPU-generated fixture bytes are not GPU pixels or a measured FPS improvement.
nativeFollowUp: A real browser/GPU must verify Three async readback, rendered HDR/ACES/sRGB equivalence, desktop/mobile camera feeds, theme changes, main-view interactions and paired frame/input timings. Sync fallback remains a compatibility path and is not claimed nonblocking.
